governance.attested_by: nyiso-72 session 2026-07-23: the nyiso-70 keeper recipe (replay_keeper.py of results/calibration/nyiso70_scr_edrp_reserve) re-solved across 2023-2025 with a SINGLE delta — gas_offer_net_revenue_margin=True (the gas-offer net-revenue margin form; charter docs/handoffs/gas-offer-net-revenue-margin-design-2026-07.md; NEISO keeper neiso-61 precedent). Each registered gas band's markup above its MEASURED physical basis (the phys_* keys on offer_curve_by_group, cited to the CAMPD marginal-HR artifact nyiso_campd_marginal_hr_summary.csv p50s) is repriced from the fuel-scaled multiplier to a FIXED $/MWh net-revenue margin at the 3.9046 $/MMBtu train-window delivered-gas anchor (GAS_OFFER_MARGIN_ANCHOR_BY_ISO['NYISO'], mean of the 2023-2025 delivered-gas overlay 3.36/2.80/5.56). At fuel==anchor the offer reduces EXACTLY to the registered multiplier; the ONLY change is the markup's gas-elasticity 1->0. ZERO new tunable: the markup LEVELS are the already-registered offer surface, the anchor is a measured delivered-gas mean, n_residual UNCHANGED at 5. 404-412 gas tranches compressed at anchor (median fixed margin 6.04 $/MWh, max 315.57 = the CT_PEAKER $-cap rung).
governance.note: BASE arm (flag off) reproduces the nyiso-70 keeper BYTE-IDENTICALLY (system-price maxDelta 0.0000 all three years) — the identification branch is default-off byte-inert. Energy dispatch under the margin is nearly unchanged (largest class shift ST_GAS -0.43..-0.50 TWh, a small within-gas-family reshuffle toward CC/CT; non-gas classes — nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, imports — identical to the byte; C1 fuel-mix and C2 volume unchanged). The margin form is the more structurally faithful offer model (real bidders express start/no-load hurdles and the scarcity wall as $ net-revenue targets, not heat-rate multiples; the multiplicative form's markup scales with the fuel bill, unidentified inside the homogeneous 2023-25 gas window and refuted by the 2022 NEISO validation rotation).
governance.residuals_note: PRE-REGISTERED REFUTATION NOT MET — promoted on EXPLICIT OWNER OVERRIDE (2026-07-23), rule 1 (most structurally faithful offer form), with the full A/B result in view. The charter keeper bar is 'MARGIN C3b <= BASE C3b EVERY year'; NYISO FAILS it: the price duration-shape NRMSE (probe scripts/probes/netrev_margin_ab.py, RT-scored) DEGRADES in ALL THREE years — 2023 0.5086->0.5260, 2024 0.3573->0.3781, 2025 0.6155->0.6385. C3a mean: 2023 +18.1%->+20.6% (already outside the +/-10% band — the known nyiso-70 2023 downstate-thermal energy-LEVEL residual, pushed further out by the below-anchor firm), 2024 +1.0%->+3.6% (in band, worse), 2025 +5.5%->+1.7% (in band, IMPROVES — the above-anchor compression). The two-sided mechanism behaves exactly as designed (firms below anchor, compresses above); it is simply the WRONG DIRECTION for NYISO's in-sample residual, whose dominant miss is the 2023 energy-LEVEL gap, not the offer form (same finding class as CAISO, whose A/B caiso-112 also degraded on 2/3 years). CONSISTENT WITH THE FINAL CAISO DECISION: CAISO was subsequently ADOPTED the same day on the same owner directive / rule 1 (origin/main 681c6de + keeper 2026-07-23-caiso-netrev-margin-keeper), so the net-revenue margin is the go-forward offer form across ISOs despite the in-sample shape cost. Promoted on the structural-form argument and its expected out-of-sample (2022/2019/H1-2026) generalization advantage over the fuel-scaled form (the NEISO rotation rationale). NO residual tuning performed — the mechanism was NOT adjusted to rescue the shape (rule 1 / pre-registered refutation). 2022 holdout NOT touched (NYISO carries no calibration-complete marker).

_open_items: (1) The margin form DEGRADES in-sample C3b in ALL THREE years (charter refutation not met); it is kept on owner override for structural fidelity, NOT because it improves the fit. The out-of-sample generalization claim — that the fuel-invariant $ margin beats the fuel-scaled multiplier on 2022/2019/H1-2026 (the NEISO rotation rationale) — is UNTESTED for NYISO and is THE open validation item; it cannot be checked until NYISO earns a calibration-complete marker (holdout quarantine, rule 22). (2) The dominant NYISO in-sample miss remains the 2023 C3a energy-LEVEL residual (+20.6%), unchanged in character from nyiso-70 and NOT an offer-form problem (candidate levers: CC/ST offer-surface level, Transco/Iroquois gas basis, neighbor import pricing); the margin makes it marginally worse in 2023 (below-anchor firm), an accepted cost of the override. (3) All nyiso-70 open items carry forward unchanged (East-side Blenheim-Gilboa PS reserve; the C7 ST_GAS 2023 off-peak shape). (4) No offer_curve_by_group residual re-tune taken (rule 22).

entries.name: nyiso_scr_edrp
entries.note: NYISO SCR/EDRP emergency demand response as endogenous per-zone price-responsive supply blocks. Capacity = Gold-Book-registered SCR+EDRP MW per model zone (2023/24/25 summer 1.23/1.29/1.49 GW, scripts/data/build_nyiso_scr_edrp.py, byte-identical to the transcribed enrollment CSV). Strike = the published NYISO EDRP $500/MWh compensation floor (Market Services Tariff §5.12) — a market-design constant, NOT a residual. Clears the energy balance only when the zone LBMP exceeds the strike (endogenous scarcity trigger, never pinned to observed event dates; rule 13/17). ZERO fitted values; re-derives for a forward year from the next Gold Book (rule 23). Excluded from generation-mix scoring (avoided load, not generation).

entries.name: nyiso_hydro_reserve_eligible
entries.note: NYISO in-fleet conventional hydro (data.hydro.build_hydro_fleet, ~4.6 GW) made eligible to supply operating reserve in BOTH the full-30min and quick-10min classes. NYPA Niagara/St-Lawrence + Capital hydro are NYISO-certified operating-reserve providers (Ancillary Services Manual); the eligibility union mirrors the CAISO _caiso_reserve_eligible hydro seam. Held reserve spends no water — the monthly hydro energy budget bounds only DISPATCHED energy, so budget and reserve headroom compose correctly. ZERO fitted value; a market-design eligibility gate, not a parameter.
